This is a hedged author cause, not an asserted cause, and no cortisol-related hypotension is stated as a separate finding.
The anchor for "Approximately 12-18 hours later" is not named; it follows the sentence about persistent headache and nausea after hydration, with no absolute time of admission stated.
Surgical decompression is only stated as the purpose of the transfer; whether it was performed and the outcome are not reported.

claims.text: A 73-year-old man with hypertension and type 2 diabetes presented with 4-5 days of vomiting, nausea, constipation and a sudden, sharp bifrontal headache rated 8/10. Initial vitals showed hypotension of 68/54 mm Hg with dry mucosa and no focal neurological deficits. CT head was unremarkable, and blood tests showed hyponatremia, hypokalemia, BUN 56 mg/dL and creatinine 3.3 mg/dL.
